comparator.name: Fiscal Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: Current adopted EB regulations and dated catalogue confirm a 180 EC Fiscal Economics degree with one 6 EC restricted elective and no formal specialisation. This supported partial record shows 177 EC and instantiates Corporate Social Responsibility in an International Context as the elective. Business Analytics is an official option but its regression preparation was not established from required-course evidence; no automatic eligibility is inferred from Quantitative Data Analysis 1. B6 lists two academic prerequisites for the compulsory 3 EC European Tax Law course, while its shared entry retains a separate minor-enrolment condition. Regular bachelor access remains unresolved.
components: Corporate Social Responsibility in an International Context
This example selects a 6 EC option on corporate responsibility, stakeholders and sustainability. The course is open to Economics and Business bachelor students.
Taxation of Directors and Major Shareholders

A 6 EC seminar develops the thesis question, research approach, introduction and first literature chapter. Entry requires completion of years one and two and at least 120 EC. Specialist tax courses are recommended preparation.

A 6 EC individual thesis follows the Fiscal Economics Graduation Seminar. Students deepen their research and analysis and submit progress reports; a final discussion may be required by the coordinator.

audience.programmeDescription: The University of Amsterdam’s Fiscal Economics bachelor combines economics, accounting and law to study taxation of households and firms, public finances and ethical questions. Students progress through specialist fiscal courses, a graduation seminar and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The table accounts for 177 EC of the 180 EC degree and includes one selected restricted elective. A complete UCR comparison awaits confirmation of regular bachelor access to the remaining compulsory 3 EC European tax law course.

curriculum.limitation: This is a partial curriculum for 2026–2027. It shows 177 EC, including the illustrated 6 EC restricted elective, and leaves out the compulsory 3 EC European tax law course while its bachelor-entry condition remains unresolved.

componentNotes.y1-orientation-econ-law: Introduces economic analysis of law and the legal constraints on economic policy, including tax law.
componentNotes.y1-foundations-1: Introduces economic and business concepts such as incentives, firms, markets, public goods and regulation, with critical reading of academic literature.
componentNotes.y1-foundations-2: Combines study and academic skills with economic, fiscal, ethical and sustainability questions about digital platforms.
componentNotes.y1-financial-accounting-1: Introduces transaction recording, accrual accounting, assets, liabilities and financial statements.
componentNotes.y1-microeconomics-1: Studies consumer and producer choices, markets, efficiency, market failure and strategic interaction.
componentNotes.y1-macroeconomics-1: Studies aggregate economic activity, banks, money, growth and business cycles using macroeconomic models.
componentNotes.y1-quantitative-analysis-1: Develops probability, statistical inference, confidence intervals and analysis of relationships using SPSS.
componentNotes.y1-finance-1: Introduces time value of money, investment appraisal, valuation, risk and return, and working-capital management.
componentNotes.y1-orientation-fiscal-econ: Introduces income, payroll, corporate, consumption, inheritance and gift taxes and their relationships.
componentNotes.y1-qualitative-project: A small-group qualitative research project investigates a problem in real organisations. Associated skills work develops Excel and presentation skills.
componentNotes.y2-general-tax: Introduces income taxation and payroll levies as preparation for advanced fiscal study.
componentNotes.y2-property-law: Studies Dutch private law, obligations, employment contracts, liability and rights over property.
componentNotes.y2-business-tax: Introduces fiscal profit determination, corporate income taxation and VAT, preparing later specialist tax courses.
componentNotes.y2-company-reporting-law: Studies partnerships and companies, governance, liability, restructuring and annual-reporting law, including commercial and fiscal accounts.
componentNotes.y2-tax-government: Examines public finance, taxation, social spending, public debt, redistribution and intergenerational questions.
componentNotes.y2-financial-accounting-2: Develops financial reporting for assets, liabilities, equity, revenue and cash flows. The programme accepts its first-year Financial Accounting 1 for Economics as preparation.
componentNotes.y2-management-accounting-1: Studies cost and performance information used for pricing, investment, planning and organisational decisions.
componentNotes.y2-financial-accounting-3: Develops advanced financial reporting, including consolidation, pensions, income taxes, leases and disclosure. Financial Accounting 2 provides recommended preparation.
componentNotes.y2-fiscal-methodology: Examines taxation as a moral phenomenon, tax principles, philosophy of science, international tax competition and professional ethics.
componentNotes.y2-tax-technology: A 3 EC course examines interactions between technology and taxation, including crypto-assets, information exchange, AI and tax policy.
componentNotes.y2-payroll-tax: A 3 EC course applies wage-tax and social-insurance rules to practical cases and employment conditions.
componentNotes.y3-bound-elective: This example selects a 6 EC option on corporate responsibility, stakeholders and sustainability. The course is open to Economics and Business bachelor students.
componentNotes.y3-tax-procedure: Studies formal obligations through the tax-return and assessment cycle, including taxpayer rights, legal protection, interest and administrative penalties.
componentNotes.y3-corporate-tax: Studies corporate taxation, including contributions and distributions, interest limitations, participation exemptions, fiscal unity and loss relief.
componentNotes.y3-vat: Develops specialist understanding of taxable transactions and deduction of input VAT.
componentNotes.y3-international-tax: Studies taxing rights, double-taxation relief, cross-border liabilities, withholding taxes and tax treaties.
componentNotes.y3-dga-tax: Studies the fiscal position of directors and major shareholders, including substantial-shareholdings, succession, payroll and transfers into a company.
componentNotes.y3-finance-2: Builds on Finance 1 to study financing and investment, valuation, capital structure, options, payout policy and governance.
componentNotes.y3-graduation-seminar: A 6 EC seminar develops the thesis question, research approach, introduction and first literature chapter. Entry requires completion of years one and two and at least 120 EC. Specialist tax courses are recommended preparation.
componentNotes.y3-profit-calculation: Studies fiscal total and annual profit and their relationship to profit measures used in financial reporting.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: A 6 EC individual thesis follows the Fiscal Economics Graduation Seminar. Students deepen their research and analysis and submit progress reports; a final discussion may be required by the coordinator.
